Hi coaches, Nikhil Jayashankar leads business development for Swing Vision. He's based in San Francisco and is a lifelong tennis player that grew up in the Bay Area and played college tennis at UC Berkeley. His responsibilities at Swing Vision include partnership and sales with clubs, academies and colleges. Nikhil works closely with coaches, clubs and college teams to enhance their services with Swing Vision. He's extremely passionate about the sport and how technology can benefit coaches and players alike. Please join me in welcoming Nikhil as he talks us through the use of Swing Vision and how it can benefit coaches, clubs and academies. Over to you Nikhil. Thanks Scott and thanks everyone for taking the time to watch this presentation. In the next 30 minutes I'll explain what Swing Vision is, the analysis the app provides and how coaches and clubs can leverage the app to create an improved experience for members and generate more revenue. Swing Vision is a mobile app that uses artificial intelligence to analyze your video in real time. It provides a variety of stats like shot placement, court positioning, shot speed and consistency

Swing Vision provides cloud storage so you can save your videos without taking up storage on your phone and allows you to share videos with others remotely. The app also allows you to challenge line calls using an Apple Watch or another iPhone or iPad. Just tap the challenge button and you can pick any shot to see a slow-mo zoomed in replay along with the app's call of whether it was in or out. Our biggest differentiator is that we're able to do all of this with just an iPhone instead of requiring dedicated camera infrastructure on your court. Using Swing Vision is the most portable, easy to use and affordable solution. To use the app, mount your phone behind one of the baselines on court, start recording and the app will analyze your video in real time without any cellular data or wifi. We suggest putting your phone in airplane mode or do not disturb so incoming calls don't interrupt your recording. When you're done playing, just take the phone down, end the recording and all the stats and video are immediately accessible. To mount your phone, we sell this extendable phone mount that sits on top of the fence and provides a good viewing angle of both the near and far side.

Optionally, you can see a preview of the camera and start the recording from an Apple Watch or spare iPhone. We also have permanent mounting solutions for clubs that make it easy for players to simply slide in their phone and use the app. Now let's talk about what you can record at Swing Vision and the analysis the app provides. To record a session in the app, visit the record tab. You'll see there are four session types to choose from. Rally is meant for live ball drills or hitting without structured point play. You can choose either singles or doubles but note that the app can only accurately track one ball being hit at a time. Match is meant for recording singles or doubles matches and can be customized to various scoring formats. Serve practice is a dedicated mode to analyze your serves, for example if you're hitting out of a basket. Finally, ball machine mode can be used if your student is hitting with a ball machine or you're feeding balls to them out of a basket. It's important to note that if you're feeding out of a basket to multiple players on the opposite side, Swing Vision doesn't currently break out the stats for each player but aggregates them instead. When choosing your session, you can tag the participating players as well as a coach. The session will then show up on each tagged person's profile under the me tab. You can also tag players or a coach after the session is complete.

After you've chosen your session type, tap the start button and you'll be taken to the recording screen. We suggest recording with the main cameras on the back of your phone for optimal results. The app will ask you to align the near service line to be inside the pink rectangle before you start recording. This is a guideline to provide the best playback angle on most courts but isn't mandatory. Ultimately, the most important consideration is to keep the court lines in view of the camera. It's okay if the edges of the near side alleys are cut off, particularly for single sessions. There are a few controls on the recording screen worth pointing out. At the top right, you'll see a slider that toggles between audio guided and manual setup. Pressing start with manual setup selected will start your recording right away. This is suggested if you know that your camera is set to the right angle. If you're unsure of the recording angle, audio guided mode provides audible feedback that lets you know if the camera needs to be adjusted. At the bottom right, you'll see a zoom control that allows you to zoom out if you need to capture more of the court. At the bottom left is a remote button that allows you to pair another iPhone or iPad to your recording device in order to see a preview of the recording screen and start the recording remotely. This will also allow you to challenge line calls on your remote device.

Below the main video player are a variety of pre-cut video clips that the app automatically generates like your 5 most tiring rallies, 5 longest rallies, rallies above 5 shots, break points, game points, and either player's forehands, backhands and serves. You can tap in to any of these thumbnails to view them. When you enter the main video player, the recording will play from beginning to end and remove all of the time in between points. This allows you to see a 2 hour match in 30 minutes or less. The app is plotting the shot placement, shot type, and shot speed on the right side of the screen.

You can tap on any stroke within the shot distribution chart, and the graphs underneath will update accordingly. Now that we know what swing vision does, let's talk about how coaches are using it. Coaches have started to use swing vision in numerous ways to enhance their services to students and generate more revenue. One of the most common use cases we see is for remote coaching. Coaches who have students that participate in junior tournaments or adult league matches are increasingly encouraging their students to record their match plate through swing vision, enabling coaches to provide feedback remotely during a tournament or after the event has ended. While it's not practical to travel to every tournament as a coach, it takes less than 30 minutes to review a student's match video and stats. Coaches recording their match can simply text or email a link to their coach for access. This saves hours of time and allows coaches to charge for remote analysis by interpreting a player's video and stats and providing feedback before their next match or practice session. Coaches are even creating their own match reports with swing vision and offering them to students as an additional service.

In 2023, we will take remote coaching a step further by leveraging our automatic distribution of match and session data to enable players anywhere in the world to connect with a network of qualified coaches. Coaches are also increasingly leveraging video and stats to provide in-person tactical lessons as a separate service to on-court coaching. Gather your student around an iPad, laptop, or TV and walk through recordings of match play or practice sessions. Swing vision makes it easy to look at point construction and matches and identify successful strategies for your student. Conversely, you'll also be able to more easily see how your player is losing points. As a coach, you'll have a better understanding of what to work on with the student in an on-court lesson. Your players will also gain helpful context in knowing what parts of their game they need to improve and why. While the concept of providing lesson videos to students as a premium package has existed for years, swing vision makes it easier than ever. Not only can you tag your student in a recording so that they have access to the video and stats, you can also filter to particular shots and provide targeted feedback. For example, if serves were a focus during a lesson, you could filter to all missed serves and send that clip to your student with some points of feedback. Where are the videos stored? After recording from an iPhone or iPad, the video is stored locally on your device. Once you're connected to Wi-Fi, leave the app open on the me tab and your videos will upload to the cloud. Once the videos have finished uploading, you can remove them from your device to save space and still always access previously recorded videos through the app. Videos will need to upload to the cloud before they can be viewed on remote devices. Does the app require cellular or Wi-Fi connection? No, your video is analyzed on device without internet. We suggest putting your phone in do not disturb or airplane mode so incoming calls don't interrupt your recording. How much battery life does swing vision use? A two hour recording on low battery mode takes about 40-50% of a phone's battery. External battery packs or portable chargers are an easy solution to extend battery life if it's a concern. Can I analyze footage recorded from other devices on swing vision? Yes, you can import pre-existing footage from a GoPro, Android or smart court into the app and receive the same output analysis. What devices support swing vision? Swing vision is supported on iPhone 8 or newer or any iPad updated to iPad OS. What devices support real time analysis? Real time analysis is supported on all devices with the A13 chip or newer. This includes the iPhone SE 2nd generation, iPhone 11 and newer, as well as any iPad Pro, iPad Air and iPad Mini released since the beginning of 2020. Older devices will process the video after it's been recorded. When will swing vision be available on Android and what can I do in the meantime? We begin development on an Android app and will launch it in summer 2023. The initial release will focus on flagship devices that are capable of running our AI in real time like the Google Pixel 6 and 7 and Samsung Galaxy S22. If you'd like to get started using swing vision right away but don't have an iPhone or an iPad, we recommend the iPhone SE 2nd generation which is currently $160 on Amazon. Thanks for tuning in.
